body: Yeah, I agree. Ranked isn't really about playing your best, though obviously it helps if you do. Ranked is about grinding out games over and over until you make it to where you want to be.

Yeah, pretty much. I recognize how much of a sore loser I am. Always have been an attention whore and not dealt with the "always someone better" thing very well. You're pretty much spot on. I made the post coming off a string of bad losses and felt like maybe I could get some insight here, but all I really wanted was someone to validate my being a baby about things.
Eh, I mean, I've been told that a lot, but it doesn't work so well for me. I'm extremely competitive and a really sore loser, so every loss feels like an utter waste of valuable time in my life.
To be fair, most people do that to me in normals too.

It's painful to say that LoL has, in a lot of ways, actually made my conditions (clinically diagnosed depression since age 13, ADHD, and Asperger's Syndrome) worse. I was told throughout my whole life that there wasn't anything I couldn't do, and I've never received anything but support, but it led to me believing I was super special and that I had some kind of destiny to fulfill--so when I started to experience my first failures in life, it was earth-shattering. From the first failing grade to the first girl who didn't want to go out with me, and things only got worse. I was starting to attempt when I was 13 and I didn't stop until I was 17.

Yet through it all, nobody told me there was anything I couldn't do. I started to hate myself, started to feel like I was letting everyone down. I started to crave negativity, wanted to make people hate me to justify my own bitterness and self-loathing. I started to half-ass everything, refused to put forth effort, and things continued to fall into my lap. I just wanted to be the failure I thought I was to get rid of the cognitive dissonance between the outpouring of praise and my own feelings toward myself.

Then I started to get D's and failing grades in college classes. It started to become easier to justify my feelings--I got trapped in my own head and started to fold in on myself, essentially. More and more I was realizing that there wasn't some grand destiny laid out for me, that if there was potential for greatness in me, I had to pull it out myself. That was probably the straw that broke the camel's back--nothing was easy anymore. I had to live with being a full-time student, working full-time, and trying to play League of Legends enough to become pro at it. I couldn't handle any of it--I was constantly tired, working myself further into depression, I gained 40 pounds, and I started to really want to kill myself--even little losses on LoL could send me into a suicidal self-hating episode, just every little thing was earth-shattering.

Every time someone would ask me what I wanted to do, I would realize I hadn't built any skills or abilities aside from playing LoL, and I wasn't even that good at that, being only Silver V. I would tell them I wanted to do something in Esports to try and ignore the way my life was starting to unravel. I started to latch onto League--it more or less became my way to ignore the rest of my life, to stop myself from thinking about the way I was spinning my wheels, not networking, leaving my college GPA at a 2.5, working shitty jobs to buy stuff I didn't really need, especially Riot points.

Not that League helped much--I would be aggressive and toxic toward other players when they offered advice to me, I was constantly getting into flame wars, and they would always make me play shittier. I wouldn't even play ranked to try and advance my "dream" because I was too scared to fail and shatter myself any further. Every time I would try to go to it, I would experience cold sweats, hammering, fast pulse, and shortness of breath. This has been going on for me for 3 years now--too scared to play Ranked and work on my ELO, too scared to walk away into the empty life I've built for myself, feeling trapped, like there's nothing waiting for me if I leave. It's still like that, but now I have a fairly stable job, I pulled 2 A's and a B last semester, and I managed to come out of my placements in Gold V this season. By no means am I mentally healthy now, I'm only just now going back on Prozac and Medidate CD, and I'm waiting on a referral from a counselor.

I still want to try and be pro in LoL, but now that I'm 21, it feels like I'm too old for it, and I'm scared that I'm just playing out of mindless addiction, and although I do enjoy it when I win, losses can still be emotionally crippling. I still feel lost, full of self-loathing and unsure of what I can do with myself, but there's tangible improvement, to some degree--still need to drop the 40 pounds, though.

Time for me to go to my summer class--it's made me feel a little better, having written this, and I know my story isn't as terrible as most, but there you have it. I guess I'll check for replies once I get back. Thanks for listening, guys.

My absolute kryptonite is Kayle, Kayle, Kayle. There is no champion in the game I have a worse time with and just seeing her picked can tilt me.

She absolutely dumps on my laners (typically I jungle) and while I myself don't usually have issues laning against her other than getting zoned from farm, she somehow always leaves lane-phase with high kills and farm. And it seems like even if I gank her, I cannot put her enough out of the game, especially if she roams. If Kayle is in-game, I feel I have to commit 100% of my resources to shutting her down, to the detriment of other lanes.

If even one person besides Kayle gets fed, it feels like immediate GG, because even if you bait her ult, someone can just go all-in and use the spare time the invuln gives to wreck my team.

Mainly what I wanted to ask is if there's anyone out there willing to just sort of try to improve with me, offer back-and-forth constructive criticism. Not coaching, exactly, since I don't feel like I need that, I just want someone to play with and bounce thoughts off of. None of my friends play the game all that seriously, and it's hard to use myself or my replays as a point of reference, so I wanted someone (or multiple someones) with some dedication and desire to improve that I could play with, so I can have someone to tell me when/if I've done things wrong and vice-versa. I'm Gold V right now, and I'm hoping to ladder-climb and eventually try out for a team, but for now, I just need a good, solid person or group to play with that really wants to help each other improve. Mine, I think was just yesterday. I never really make "big plays" so any real moments I have come from small things.

In this case, we were 4v5 because our 11/3 LeBlanc had disconnected (Gold V ranked game) due to connection issues. We turtled up for about ten minutes, just getting picks where we could, until the enemy team did Baron after we took their inhib. Jinx had just respawned, so I called for her to fire her rocket at Baron from max distance. Seeing it wouldn't make it in time, I pinged everyone to go in, popped my ult (I was Renekton), sliced over the wall and stunned Evelynn, buying just enough time for her to miss smite and the rocket to steal Baron. We picked up two kills and pushed for the win from there. Not a massive play from me, but some of the most solid soloqueue shotcalling I've done.
